Kūrattālvār,_kūranātha,_kūreśa
or zrIvatsAGka of Hārīta gotra; son of Rāmamiśra; disciple an. contemporary of Rāmānujācārya; born in 1039 A. D. in the Agrahāra called Kūram near Kāñcī, held some authority over the place an. hence the names Kūranātha etc; lived in Srirangam; father of Parāśara Bhaṭṭa (a. of Aṣṭaślokī; Śrīguṇaratnakośa, Oxf. 130a, etc.) an. great grandfather of Sudarśana (a. of C. Śrutaprakāśikā on Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya); said to have defeated the Śaivas in debate in the court of the Col. King Kulottuṅga I. See below Kūreśavijaya. For a. account of his life see Sahṛdaya, XVII. 65. 89. 113. 130.
--[Kūreśavijaya. see below. Contains some verses said to have been uttered by Kūrattālvār in the court of the Col. king].
--Kūreśavijñāpana (with C.). a cryptic message in 3 verses, on Śrīvaiṣṇavism, said to have been sent by Kūrattālvār. MD. 5232 (inc.).
--Nārāyaṇāṣṭaka. 8 verses; (beg. vAtsalyAdabhayapradAnasamayAd; this verse is found also in Mukundamālā); these verses [Page263-b] are found in the beg. of Ārttatrāṇaparāyaṇastotra. a.. MD. 9871 etc. (See NCC. II. p. 166, Ārttatrāṇanārāyaṇastotra, Adyar I. p. 198a which is the same work).

--Pañcastava(-v.). Collection of five stotras, Atimānuṣastava (NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 98), Varadarājastava, Vaikuṇṭhastava, Śrīstava(-stuti) an. Sundarabāhustava.

Kūrmapurāṇa
one of the 18 Mahāpurāṇas; imparted by Viṣṇu in his incarnation a. a tortoise to King Indradyumna. According to the Bhāgavata, Vāyu an. Matsya Purāṇas, it contained 17000 or 18000 ślokas; but the extant text has only 6000. According to the ptd. text (I. p. 4, Bib. Ind. edn.), Kū. p.. consisted of four Saṁhitās, Brāhmī, Bhāgavatī, Saurī an. Vaiṣṇavī; an. the available text represents the first only. The Nāradīya p.. (pūrva. 106. 1-2) gives the contents of the three other Saṁhitās, their extent being respectively 4000, 2000 an. 5000 granthas. See Wilson, Viṣṇu p.. I. Preface p.. lxxvi-viii. Its date is probably 500-800 A. D. (R. C. Hazra, Puranic Records on Hindu rites an. customs p. 71). On dh. writers who q. it from 1060 A. D. onwards an. its Smṛti chs., see R. C. Hazra, ibid. p.. 66, 71-75. For a review of its contents, see Mm. Pt. Giridhar Sharma Caturvedi, Purāṇa III. 1961, p.. 235-52. See also ‘Kū. p.. Concordance’ by Sri Ram [Page266-a. Shankar Bhattacarya, Purāṇa III. 1961, p.. 333-96.
